effects: Takes exactly `assets` XAUt from the signer to the vault with safeTransferFrom (enter), which uses up the signer's XAUt allowance to the vault.
Mints vault shares to `onBehalf`. The share count comes from previewDeposit at the current share price, and the code sets no minimum.
Moves the deposited XAUt into the liquidity adapter (allocateInternal). This is between other parties and does not change what the signer gets.
Accrues interest first and may mint fee shares to the fee recipients, which dilutes the share price used for the mint.
formats.shown: Deposit 0.01 XAUt for the onBehalf address, with a field naming the share ticker tsXAUT and the address that receives the shares.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted is not shown; the vault computes it and sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The descriptor field 'Share ticker' (raw constant tsXAUT) shows only the ticker. Case 0 minted 0.01 shares to 0xdead.

findings.title: deposit: the XAUt allowance used by the transferFrom is not mentioned; this is the prerequisite of a deposit.
findings.evidence: Case 0 has an approval effect XAUt signer→vault, amount 0, signer 'grant' (allowance used up). Code: enter `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`.

findings.title: deposit: the hard-coded share ticker tsXAUT differs from the symbol xaueXAUT on the receipt's share transfers.
findings.evidence: descriptor metadata.constants.vaultTicker "tsXAUT" shown as 'Share ticker'. In case 0 the share mint effect has symbol "xaueXAUT" (asset 0x98b1…c443).
findings.fix: Use the vault's on-chain symbol, or confirm that tsXAUT is current.

cases.notes: 0.01 XAUt out is shown exactly. Shares go to 0xdead, and the reader saw that correctly. The allowance used up is not on the screen.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Sends exactly `assets` XAUt from the vault to `receiver`.
Burns vault shares from `onBehalf`. The share count comes from previewWithdraw (rounded up), and the code sets no maximum.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, it uses up the signer's share allowance from onBehalf by the number of shares burned.
May pull liquidity from the liquidity adapter. This is between other parties.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 1.75 XAUt to the receiver, with the Owner field naming whose shares are used.

findings.title: withdraw: the screen never says the owner's vault shares are burned to pay for the XAUt.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. Case 1: 1.748418276912008019 xaueXAUT left the signer (signer out). The screen has only 'Withdraw exactly 1.75 XAUt', To and Owner. The reader wrote 'the screen doesn't say what form it leaves in'.
findings.fix: Say it in the intent or a label, e.g. intent 'Withdraw XAUt by burning tsXAUT shares', label 'Owner (shares burned)'.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of shares burned is not shown; the vault computes it and sets no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. There is no maxShares parameter.

findings.title: withdraw: the sentence leaves out the owner whose shares are spent, which matters when the owner is not the signer.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent "Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}". onBehalf is shown only as the 'Owner' field. exit spends `allowance[onBehalf][msg.sender]` when msg.sender != onBehalf.

cases.notes: 1.75 XAUt in to the signer is shown exactly. The burn of 1.7484 shares is not stated as a share burn, and the reader only knew the position shrank.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` vault shares from `onBehalf`. When the signer is not onBehalf, this uses up the signer's share allowance.
Sends XAUt to `receiver`. The amount comes from previewRedeem at the current share price, and the code sets no minimum.
May pull liquidity from the liquidity adapter. This is between other parties.
formats.shown: Redeem 0.1973 tsXAUT shares to the receiver, with the Owner field; nothing says what asset comes back or how much.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says the signer receives XAUt; the reader could only guess the asset.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` where asset is XAUt. Case 1 of this format (index 2): 0.19734 XAUt in to the signer. The screen has only 'Shares to redeem', To and Owner. The reader wrote 'Some underlying asset (likely XAUT)... amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Name the output, e.g. intent 'Redeem tsXAUT for XAUt', or add a constant field 'Receive' = $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker.

findings.title: redeem: the XAUt amount received is not shown; the vault computes it and sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. There is no minAssets parameter.

findings.title: redeem: the share symbol shown, tsXAUT, differs from the symbol xaueXAUT on the receipt.
findings.evidence: Case 2 screen: '0.19725630751572786 tsXAUT'. The mined share burn effect has symbol "xaueXAUT".

cases.notes: Shares out are shown exactly. The XAUt received (0.19734) has neither asset nor amount on the screen.
